correctness.rationale: The opposite-facet barycentric identity gives the exact outer-simplex gauge in every vertex-opposite direction. Inclusion reverses gauges and central symmetry identifies the norms of p_i and -p_i. The reciprocal Cauchy inequality then proves the universal d(d+1) bound. For K=Delta-Delta, the average-of-the-other-vertices identity and a centered barycentric linear functional give both containment and exact norm d for every vertex of (d+1)Delta. No infinite claim depends on finite computation.
risks: The result concerns the d+1-vertex restriction, not unrestricted vein(K).

originality.rationale: Bezdek--Litvak record d(d+1) only for Euclidean simplices circumscribing the Euclidean ball and separately pose the three-dimensional T-T equality conjecture. Gluskin--Litvak prove an unrestricted 2d lower bound and a more general but weaker d+k vertex average-asymmetry estimate; their stated d+1 vertex inequality does not imply the present exact normed result. Candidate-specific searches found no statement extending the Euclidean simplex bound to every centrally symmetric unit ball or identifying the exact simplex-restricted T-T cost.
residual_risks: An equivalent barycentric lemma may exist in older Minkowski-asymmetry literature without vertex-index terminology.
The unrestricted vertex index of T-T in dimension three is not resolved by this result.
The Euclidean d(d+1) circumscribing-simplex case is explicitly prior-covered and is not claimed as new.

value.rationale: The d+1-vertex restriction is the smallest possible outer-polytope regime in the vertex-index definition. Determining it sharply is structurally meaningful because the motivating three-dimensional conjecture predicts the same total cost 12 on T-T; the theorem proves that value is already unavoidable and attainable for every tetrahedral outer approximation, so any failure of the unrestricted equality must use at least five vertices. The all-dimensional d(d+1) theorem and the Delta-Delta equality family are natural finite-complexity benchmarks rather than arbitrary slices.
risks: The value lies in a restricted approximation class and should not be presented as resolving the full conjecture.
